steps.title: Prepare Buffers and Reagents
steps.instruction: Prepare the necessary buffers and extraction solutions.

substeps.instruction: Prepare 100 mM pH 7 Tris buffer: Dilute 1 part 1M pH 7 Tris (Fisher Scientific #BP1756-500) with 9 parts MilliQ.
Prepare 50 mM pH 7 Tris buffer: Dilute 5 parts 1M pH 7 Tris with 95 parts MilliQ.
Prepare Protein Extraction Buffer (PEB, 1X): Combine 2% SDS, 10% glycerol, and 5 mM EDTA in 100 mM pH 7 Tris buffer.
To make PEB 1X from 4X: Mix 1 part PEB (4X) with 3 parts 100 mM pH 7 Tris buffer.
Prepare 4% PEB Mix: Mix 1.6 mL PEB (1X) with 38.4 mL MilliQ.
Prepare Re-solubilization buffer (RSB): Add 500 µL 20% sarcosine into 9.5 mL 50 mM Tris.
Prepare PEB stock components: Add 40 g glycerol (Bioshop #GLY001.500) and 4 mL 0.5 M EDTA (Merck #4055-100ml) to a 100 mL bottle, then top to 100 g with 100 mM pH 7 Tris buffer.

steps.title: Sample Collection and Preparation
steps.instruction: Collect microalgae and prepare samples for homogenization.

substeps.instruction: Rinse filter tunnel with filtered artificial seawater (nutrient free).
Filter microalgae in liquid media onto filters using gentle vacuum pressure (130 mmHg). Use GF/F filters for higher protein recovery.
Filter blank media (without cells) through a polycarbonate filter as a blank.
Fold the filter using rinsed forceps: (1) Fold in half along diameter to a semicircle; (2) Fold again into a long strip; (3) For polycarbonate, fold once more to halve length.
Place folded filter in a 2 mL cryogenic vial.
For freeze-dried samples: Grind in metal grinding tubes (MPBio 116992006) using dry ice and a CoolPrep adapter on a FastPrep-24 5G.

steps.title: Homogenization and Extraction
steps.instruction: Extract proteins using a bead beater and centrifugation.

substeps.instruction: Transfer samples/filters into Lysing matrix tubes (containing 1.4 mm ceramic, 0.1 mm silica, and one 4 mm glass bead). For folded filters, unfold to a strip before inserting into the bead mixture.
Reverse pipet 1 mL PEB (1X) into each bead tube.
Place bead tubes on ice. Remove samples from ULT and keep on ice.
Ensure caps are tightly closed and log tube positions.
Run FastPrep-24 5G for 8 cycles of 00:01:00 at 6.5 m/s, checking labels between each run.
Centrifuge the extract at 20,000 rcf, 4 °C for 5 minutes using a refrigerated centrifuge (Eppendorf 5430 R) to de-foam.
Transfer extract to 2 mL microtubes and freeze aliquots at -80 °C.

steps.title: Protein Precipitation (Optional)
steps.instruction: Perform protein precipitation for specific assay requirements.

substeps.instruction: Thaw protein extract.
Add 300 µL MilliQ into each tube with extract and vortex until milky.
Gently vortex for 30 seconds using a tube insert.
Incubate in the fridge for 30 minutes.
In a fume hood, remove the upper phase (~700 µL) without disturbing the interphase.
In a fume hood, add 300 µL methanol and invert gently.
In a fume hood, remove all solvent using a 100 µL pipet tip, ensuring protein pellets remain.
Dry pellet in a vacuum desiccator for 15 minutes at room temperature with the lid open.
Flash-freeze tubes with liquid nitrogen and store at -80 °C.
Reverse pipet 100 µL RSB into tubes with precipitated protein and vortex for complete re-solubilization.
If using 4X PEB, shake at 37 °C until SDS is fully dissolved.

steps.title: Micro BCA Assay Preparation
steps.instruction: Prepare standards and working reagent for the Micro BCA assay.

substeps.instruction: Prepare BSA standards: Transfer 800 µL 2 mg/mL BSA (Thermo #0023210) to a microtube. Use reverse pipetting to transfer 100 µL into new tubes to create a series (PS2 to PS8).
Prepare crude protein standards (C1-C11) and precipitated standards (P1-P8) according to the provided dilution table using PEB, MilliQ, and BSA.
Calculate total Working Reagent (WR) volume: (# standards + # samples) X 200 µL (plus several mL extra).
Prepare WR: Mix 200 parts Micro BCA reagent A, 192 parts Reagent B, and 8 parts Reagent C in a 15 or 50 mL falcon tube.

steps.title: Micro BCA Assay Execution
steps.instruction: Perform the Micro BCA assay on a microplate.

substeps.instruction: Dispense 100 µL of WR into each well of a 96-well polystyrene clear microplate using a stepper pipette, avoiding contact with the solution.
Load 100 µL of diluted extract (extract + 288 µL MQ) into the microplate in duplicate.
Cover with lid, shake and incubate at 37 °C for 2 hours at 150 rpm.
Shake for 5 s at 600 rpm in continuous high force mode.
Read endpoint absorbance at 562 nm (measurement time 100 ms) using a Varioskan LUX reader.

steps.title: Standard BCA Assay Execution
steps.instruction: Perform the standard BCA assay for higher concentrations.

substeps.instruction: Calculate WR volume: (# standards + # samples) X 800 µL (plus several mL extra).
Prepare WR: Mix 50 parts BCA reagent A with 1 part BCA Reagent B.
Add 800 µL WR to each tube using reverse pipetting.
Vortex, shake, and incubate at 37 °C for 30 minutes at 200 rpm.
Centrifuge at 13,300 rpm at room temperature for 5 minutes.

steps.title: Data Analysis and Calculation
steps.instruction: Calculate protein concentration from absorbance data.

substeps.instruction: Subtract average absorbance of blank standard replicates from all standards.
Subtract average absorbance of blank sample (filter) replicates from all samples.
Create a response curve (Abs 562 nm vs concentration in mg/mL).
Use a quadratic curve (Abs = aConc^2 + bConc + c) for crude protein 40-400 µg/mL, or a linear curve (Abs = aConc + b) for 0-40 µg/mL.
Determine sample concentration; if below L-LOD, report as '<LOD'.
Calculate total protein per filter: Protein_mg/filter = Protein_mg/mL X PEB_mL X DF (DF=25 for Micro BCA, DF=1 for precipitated protein).
For 205 nm readings, plot Absorbance vs concentration; ensure R^2 > 0.99.
